title: NPE in SimpleAmqpHeaderMapper.toHeaders when AMQP message priority is null
errorSample:
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "java.lang.Integer.intValue()" because "priority" is null
	at org.springframework.amqp.support.SimpleAmqpHeaderMapper.toHeaders(SimpleAmqpHeaderMapper.java:155) ~[spring-amqp-4.0.0.jar:4.0.0]
	at org.springframework.amqp.support.SimpleAmqpHeaderMapper.toHeaders(SimpleAmqpHeaderMapper.java:57) ~[spring-amqp-4.0.0.jar:4.0.0]

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: Consuming a RabbitMQ message that has no priority property (for example one published from the management UI) fails in the listener container with a NullPointerException in SimpleAmqpHeaderMapper.toHeaders.
cause: In 4.0.0 the header mapper compares the nullable Integer priority with 0 (priority > 0) without a null check, so unboxing a null priority throws. Messages built via RabbitTemplate usually carry priority 0, which hides the problem.
fixSummary: Maintainers confirmed the regression and scheduled the fix for the 4.0.1 release. Until then, make sure published messages carry an explicit priority.
notes: The interim advice to set an explicit priority is an inference from the cause, not stated in the thread.

cause: The reporter traced it to unwrapped properties being removed from the internal property array while a loop in BeanPropertyMap still indexes into it, producing an index mismatch. A maintainer confirmed it as a bug.

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: JmsClient.destination("queue").sendAndReceive(payload, headers, ResponseType.class) throws IllegalStateException "No 'defaultDestination' configured" even though a destination was set; the overload without headers works.
cause: JmsMessagingTemplate overrides the convertSendAndReceive variant without headers to fall back to the default destination name, but not the variant that takes a headers map, so the inherited AbstractMessagingTemplate version only checks defaultDestination.
fixSummary: Fixed in Spring Framework 7.0.3 by overriding the missing method. Before upgrading, calling the overload without a headers map avoids the failure.

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: With TestNG parallel=methods, tests extending AbstractTestNGSpringContextTests fail randomly with "The exception was thrown with the wrong message", and a failure shows the stack trace of a different test method.
cause: AbstractTestNGSpringContextTests keeps the tracked test exception in a field of the shared test instance. TestNG runs several methods concurrently on the same instance, so one thread overwrites the exception recorded by another.
fixSummary: Fixed in Spring Framework 6.2.12 and main; upgrade spring-test.

	at org.springframework.batch.core.job.AbstractJob.stopObservation(AbstractJob.java:370)

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: Following the reference-documentation tracing example and registering only a TracingAwareMeterObservationHandler creates no spans and makes JobLauncher.run() throw IllegalArgumentException when the job observation stops.
cause: TracingAwareMeterObservationHandler is a decorator whose onStop requires a TracingContext that only a span-producing TracingObservationHandler puts into the observation context. Registered by itself it never gets one.
fixSummary: Also register a span-producing handler such as DefaultTracingObservationHandler(tracer) on the ObservationRegistry; a pull request updated the documentation example to register both handlers.
notes: The issue is tracked against milestone 6.1.0-M2; whether and where a backport landed is not established here.

symptom: After moving to Spring Boot 4 / Jackson 3, serializing a Kotlin object that has a non-null @JvmInline value class property backed by String throws ClassCastException in StringSerializer.isEmpty when the mapper uses JsonInclude.Include.NON_EMPTY as the default value inclusion.

symptom: In a native image built with Boot 4.0.3, an @ImportHttpServices client ignores spring.http.serviceclient.<group>.base-url and fails on the first call with IllegalArgumentException "URI with undefined scheme"; the JVM run works.
cause: Runtime reflection hints for binding the HTTP client properties (HttpClientProperties) were missing in the native image, so the configuration was not bound.
fixSummary: Maintainers confirmed missing hints and gave a workaround: add @ImportRuntimeHints with a RuntimeHintsRegistrar that calls BindableRuntimeHintsRegistrar.forTypes(HttpClientProperties.class).registerHints(...). A proper fix was left to a later release.
notes: The release containing the fix was not named in the thread. The issue is tracked against milestone 4.0.4; whether and where a backport landed is not established here.

errorSample:

schema_reference.4: Failed to read schema document
'https://www.liquibase.org/xml/ns/dbchangelog/dbchangelog-4.9.xsd', because
1) could not find the document; 2) the document could not be read;
3) the root element of the document is not <xsd:schema>.

appliesTo.versions: any version that fetches XSDs over the network (4.9.0 reported); server-side issue from about 2026-07-18

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: Changelog parsing fails with ChangeLogParseException "Failed to read schema document ... root element of the document is not xsd:schema" because the XSD request gets an HTTP 403 page instead of the schema.
cause: After the liquibase.org site moved behind a new CDN/security provider, its default bot protection blocked requests whose User-Agent starts with Java/, so JVM clients that download the XSD over the network received an error page.
fixSummary: Liquibase maintainers allowed Java user agents again on the site, so no client change is needed. Newer Liquibase releases resolve schemas from the distribution locally, which avoids the network dependency; a commenter suggested serving XSDs from a caching proxy.
notes: Site-side incident, mostly relevant to old Liquibase versions or liquibase.secureParsing=false.

title: BeanCurrentlyInCreationException with global lazy init and @Bean(bootstrap = BACKGROUND)
errorSample:

	at org.springframework.beans.factory.support.DefaultListableBeanFactory.checkMergedBeanDefinition(DefaultListableBeanFactory.java:1051) ~[spring-beans-7.0.7.jar:7.0.7]
	at org.springframework.beans.factory.support.AbstractBeanFactory.doGetBean(AbstractBeanFactory.java:297) ~[spring-beans-7.0.7.jar:7.0.7]

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: With spring.main.lazy-initialization=true, a @Bean(bootstrap = Bean.Bootstrap.BACKGROUND) method inside a @Configuration class logs BeanCurrentlyInCreationException: bean marked for mainline initialization but requested in background thread.
cause: Global lazy initialization makes the @Configuration class lazy, while the @Bean method is scheduled on a background thread; the background thread then needs the configuration class as factory bean, which trips the mainline/background initialization check. A maintainer reproduced it with Spring Framework alone using @Lazy on the configuration class.
fixSummary: Maintainers listed ways to avoid it: add @DependsOn for the configuration class, declare the background @Bean method static, or remove @Lazy from the configuration class. A change to Boot's lazy-initialization post-processor was only discussed.
notes: The issue is tracked against milestone 7.0.8; whether and where a backport landed is not established here.

symptom: A native image with a NewTopic bean fails at startup with ExceptionInInitializerError caused by ConfigException: class org.apache.kafka.common.security.oauthbearer.DefaultJwtValidator could not be found, while the JVM run works.

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: Reading the last job execution fails with RuntimeException caused by ClassNotFoundException: long in JdbcJobExecutionDao.getJobParameters when a parameter was added with a primitive type such as Long::class.java.
cause: The type is stored with Class.getName(), which yields "long" for a primitive class, but it is read back with Class.forName, which cannot resolve primitive type names.
fixSummary: A maintainer confirmed the bug and said the fix (resolve with ClassUtils.forName) ships in 6.0.6.
notes: The issue is tracked against milestone 6.1.0-M2; whether and where a backport landed is not established here.

title: Stored procedure OUT parameter not available outside a transaction
errorSample:
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: OUT/INOUT parameter not available: outParam
	at org.springframework.orm.jpa.SharedEntityManagerCreator$DeferredQueryInvocationHandler.invoke(SharedEntityManagerCreator.java:553)

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: Calling a stored procedure through a shared EntityManager without an active transaction (for example Spring Data JPA @Procedure with outputParameterName on @Async or @Scheduled threads) throws IllegalArgumentException "OUT/INOUT parameter not available" after the procedure has already run.
cause: In SharedEntityManagerCreator.DeferredQueryInvocationHandler a 7.0.9 rework moved the recording of registered OUT/INOUT parameters into an else-if chain; Hibernate's registerStoredProcedureParameter returns this, so the first branch always matches and the recording branch is never reached.
fixSummary: Fixed in 7.0.10 by making the recording an independent if block. Staying on 7.0.8 avoids the regression.

symptom: Deserializing a double from the string "+INF" or "+Infinity" (as produced by XML schema serializers) throws InvalidFormatException, although INF, Infinity, -INF and -Infinity are accepted.

symptom: Loading a Kotlin class whose private primary constructor takes value-class parameters (no default values) fails with MappingInstantiationException caused by IllegalArgumentException: object is not an instance of declaring class.
cause: KotlinInstantiationDelegate assumes the synthetic default-argument constructor always has both an int mask and a DefaultConstructorMarker parameter; for a private constructor without defaults the compiler emits only the marker variant, so the wrong constructor is resolved.
fixSummary: A maintainer agreed with the analysis and fixed it by also considering the original constructor as resolution target when no defaulting is involved. Giving a constructor parameter a default value avoids the failing path.
notes: The default-value workaround is inferred from the reporter's observation that a variant with a default parameter works. The release containing the fix was not stated. The issue is tracked against milestone 3.5.6 (2025.0.6); whether and where a backport landed is not established here.

title: AtomicMoveNotSupportedException Invalid cross-device link moving Gradle transforms workspace in Docker
errorSample:
Caused by: java.nio.file.AtomicMoveNotSupportedException: /app/.gradle/caches/8.14/transforms/3b2d455af66406b61ef3b1a0ba7fde4e -> /app/.gradle/caches/8.14/transforms/3b2d455af66406b61ef3b1a0ba7fde4e-e9295ee8-c0d8-42ee-bb4a-cb05bb560ad4: Invalid cross-device link
        at org.gradle.internal.execution.steps.AssignImmutableWorkspaceStep.moveInconsistentImmutableWorkspaceToTemporaryLocation(AssignImmutableWorkspaceStep.java:191)

appliesTo.versions: 8.14 reported; fix attributed to a change shipped in 9.4.0 (see notes)

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: Inside a Docker container using a cache from an earlier image layer, the build fails with "Could not move inconsistent immutable workspace" caused by AtomicMoveNotSupportedException: Invalid cross-device link.
cause: Gradle moves an inconsistent immutable workspace in the caches/transforms directory with an atomic move; the layered Docker file system does not support atomic moves across image layers even though they are the same physical device.
fixSummary: The issue was closed by Gradle change 36227. A maintainer also mentioned a lock-based approach (as used on Windows) as a possible alternative to atomic moves in the 9.x line.
notes: Another Gradle issue states change 36227 is included in 9.4.0, so 9.4.0 is the inferred fixed version. The thread offers no user-side workaround.

title: ModuleVersionNotFoundException for gradle-<version>-src.zip with local or offline distributionUrl in IDE sync
errorSample:
Caused by: org.gradle.internal.resolve.ModuleVersionNotFoundException: Could not find gradle:gradle:9.4.0-rc-1.
Searched in the following locations:
  - file:/home/user/Code/temp/sync-fail/gradle-9.4.0-rc-1-src.zip

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: IDE sync logs ModuleVersionNotFoundException "Could not find gradle:gradle:9.4.0-rc-1" looking for gradle-9.4.0-rc-1-src.zip next to a file-based distribution URL while resolving Gradle sources.
cause: Starting with 9.4.0-RC1 the Gradle sources distribution URL is derived from the distributionUrl setting instead of always using the public services host, so a locally served -bin.zip needs a matching -src.zip beside it.
fixSummary: Place the matching -src.zip next to the binary distribution (or download it there). Maintainers noted that sync itself still succeeds with a logged warning, and considered falling back to the previous behavior for non-http distribution URLs.
notes: Whether the fallback was implemented was not confirmed in the thread. A related local-build case needs GRADLE_VERSION_OVERRIDE set.

title: NoClassDefFoundError JsonProcessingException in Spring Cloud Gateway Server MVC with Spring Boot 4
errorSample:
Caused by: java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: com/fasterxml/jackson/core/JsonProcessingException
	at org.springframework.cloud.gateway.server.mvc.filter.FilterFunctions.removeResponseHeader(FilterFunctions.java:137) ~[spring-cloud-gateway-server-webmvc-5.0.0.jar:5.0.0]
	at java.base/jdk.internal.reflect.DirectMethodHandleAccessor.invoke(DirectMethodHandleAccessor.java:103) ~[na:na]

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: Gateway Server MVC 5.0.0 on Spring Boot 4 fails at startup with NoClassDefFoundError: com/fasterxml/jackson/core/JsonProcessingException from FilterFunctions.removeResponseHeader.
cause: The gateway filter functions still reference Jackson 2 classes (com.fasterxml.jackson), while Spring Boot 4 ships Jackson 3 by default.
fixSummary: Workaround from the reporter: add the spring-boot-jackson2 dependency so Jackson 2 classes are on the classpath. The thread does not state a release that removes the Jackson 2 usage.
notes: No maintainer comment in the thread; workaround is user-reported and fixed version unknown. The issue is tracked against milestone 5.0.1; whether and where a backport landed is not established here.

title: FlatFileItemReader builder fails with A name is required when saveState is true
errorSample: Caused by: org.springframework.beans.BeanInstantiationException: Failed to instantiate [org.springframework.batch.infrastructure.item.file.FlatFileItemReader]: Factory method 'reader' threw exception with message: A name is required when saveState is set to true.

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: Building a FlatFileItemReader via its builder without calling name() fails with BeanInstantiationException: "A name is required when saveState is set to true".
cause: A maintainer found that ItemStreamSupport already defaults the name to the bean name, but several builders add their own redundant Assert.hasText on a local name field that is null unless name(...) is called, so they fail before the component is created.
fixSummary: The agreed fix is to remove the redundant assertion from the affected builders. Until then, call .name("...") on the builder.
notes: The interim advice to call name() is an inference from the error message. The issue is tracked against milestone 6.1.0-M2; whether and where a backport landed is not established here.
